solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Second glutton goes round smart hotel displaying fizz

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a pig is a greedy eater
the Ritz is a famously smart London hotel

explanation.surface: A greedy diner circles a posh hotel bar, showing off a glass of something sparkling.
explanation.walkthrough: The glutton wraps itself round the hotel, and the second sits in front of the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Spritzig is a wine term borrowed from German for slightly sparkling, so such a wine shows fizz.

clue.text: Venue for classical lectures leads to serious talks on Athens

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the initials of these four words

explanation.surface: A programme of weighty discussions about Athens begins in a lecture hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition fits the wordplay neatly: the Stoics took their name from the Athenian porch where Zeno taught.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa was a roofed colonnade in ancient Greece, the porch where philosophers such as Zeno taught.

clue.text: Old-style homily directed downward

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an obsolete word for a sermon read in church
second meaning: lying face down or tending downwards

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is archaic, from the French prône, a short sermon; 'Old-style' flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an obsolete noun for a sermon and the everyday adjective for facing or sloping downwards.

clue.text: A nice walk? Eric's last as leader maybe

indicators.note: the final letter is to be moved up to stand at the front

parts.note: Eric Ambler was the English thriller writer, so his surname is his last name

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a pleasant stroll might be led by Eric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eric's last' looks like a final letter, C, but it means Eric's last name, AMBLER; 'maybe' marks him as one example of an Eric. Move its last letter R to the front for RAMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramble is a leisurely country walk taken for pleasure, which the question mark offers as one example.

clue.text: Phosphorus in mine dug out called into question

indicators.note: one element is placed inside the other
earth that is dug out is turned over and scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A miner's find of phosphorus is doubted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug out' reads as mining work, but it shuffles the two words before it; the P then goes inside after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim is to challenge its truth, so an impugned statement has been challenged.

clue.text: Love scraping by in economical dairy farming

parts.note: love is a nil score in tennis
to graze is to scrape lightly past something

explanation.surface: A dairy farmer barely scraping by while running things on the cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scraping by' suggests making ends meet, which suits the surface, but here it means brushing past.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero-grazing is a system where cut grass is brought to housed cattle instead of letting them roam, saving pasture.

clue.text: Old monarch covers self-confidence in warm coat

indicators.note: in a down entry, what covers sits on top, so it comes first

parts.note: Georgius Rex, King George, as on old pillar boxes
ego is one's sense of self-worth

explanation.surface: An elderly king's self-assurance is wrapped up in a cosy overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' looks like a container signal, but in this down light it puts the king above the self-confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A grego is a short hooded cloak of thick cloth worn in the Levant, hence a warm garment.

clue.text: Have another go at doctrine lacking leader

indicators.note: without its leader a word loses its first letter

parts.note: a credo is a creed or set of beliefs

explanation.surface: A party tries again at its beliefs now that it has no leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo something is to do it again, which is having another attempt at it.

clue.text: Unhealthy swelling became deadly in part? It must be lifted

indicators.note: lifting in a down entry means reading the letters upwards, back to front
only a part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A swelling that turned partly fatal must be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the two words and read upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Edema, the American spelling of oedema, is an abnormal build-up of fluid causing swelling.

clue.text: The old justify varied reading

indicators.note: something varied has been altered, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Elders defend a different interpretation of a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks the definition as archaic, not a group of elderly people.
explanation.definitionFit: Deraign is an obsolete legal verb meaning to vindicate or prove a claim, an old-time way to justify.

clue.text: Specialized orchard park officer placed in old yard

indicators.note: something placed in another thing sits inside it

parts.note: O for old and Y for yard, both standard abbreviations
a park ranger looks after a park

explanation.surface: A park warden is posted to an old yard to tend a specialist fruit garden.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glasshouse or grove for growing orange trees, a specialised kind of orchard.

clue.text: Shaft attached to front of favourite bit of gym equipment

indicators.note: being fixed at the front means coming first

parts.note: tram is an old word for the shaft of a cart or barrow
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A pole is fixed to the front of a favourite piece of gym kit.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAM here is not a streetcar but the shaft of a cart, a sense found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampet is a small trampoline used by gymnasts for springing into vaults.

clue.text: Lo, cheer reverberated in outing that recalls French flag?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside another word

parts.note: a tour is a trip or outing

indicators.note: sound that reverberates bounces about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Cheers echo during a trip to France, bringing the tricolour to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUR splits round the jumbled letters. The definition is adjectival: describing something with three colours.
explanation.definitionFit: The French flag is the tricolore, with three vertical bands, so a three-colour design calls it to mind.

clue.text: Extra attachment for jockey

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a clause added to a document or bill
second meaning: one who sits on a horse

explanation.surface: A spare fitting is needed for the jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is both an additional clause appended to a contract and a person on horseback, as a jockey is.

clue.text: Sound of band, not amateur, showing enthusiasm?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for amateur is taken away

parts.note: the rhythmic noise of a brass band
A is a standard abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: A professional band's sound shows real gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of band' is not a homophone signal; it is the noise itself, minus one A.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for energy, vigour or zest, which is close to enthusiasm.

clue.text: Climber, male, read ranges abroad

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: roaming far from home suggests the letters wander out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mountaineer, a well-read man, travels widely overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' looks like a mountaineer but is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedera is the botanical genus of ivy, a plant that climbs walls and trees.

clue.text: Metal worker, enthusiast about gold stone

indicators.note: to be about something is to be around it

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
or is gold in heraldry
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A metalsmith who is keen on gold and gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: A forgeman is a smith working at a forge, shaping hot metal.

clue.text: Discontinued currency unit mostly originated including pound

indicators.note: one piece takes another inside it
most but not all of the word is used, so its tail goes

parts.note: to originate is to begin
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An obsolete coin mostly started life including a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' here is the money abbreviation from Latin libra, not a verb meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The belga was a Belgian unit of currency for foreign exchange, worth five francs, now no longer used.

clue.text: Pressure regulator to secure toast when it's done?

parts.note: to bar a door is to secure it

indicators.note: something done is cooked, and cooking changes its form, so the letters change order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook wants a gauge to hold the toast once it's ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done' suggests the toast is finished, but it means cooked and so rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A barostat is a device that keeps the air pressure in a chamber constant, so it regulates pressure.

clue.text: Pale? A lot, tee I mishit

indicators.note: a ball struck badly goes astray, so the letters go astray too

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer goes white after a lot of fluffed tee shots.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the answer is the verb: to pale or blanch.
explanation.definitionFit: To etiolate is to make or become pale, as plants grown without light blanch.

clue.text: Where attention is focussed, a hundred and others mature (11, two words)

parts.note: cent is from Latin for a hundred
the rest are the others
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: The spotlight falls on a centenarian among others growing older.
explanation.definitionFit: Centre stage is the middle of a theatre stage, and figuratively the position of greatest prominence.

clue.text: Accountant having to accept a stigma as bitter tonic?

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in

parts.note: a chartered accountant
a scar is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: A disgraced accountant must swallow a bitter pill.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is fair: cascara is a laxative more than a tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: Cascara sagrada is a bitter bark extract taken as a purgative medicine.

clue.text: Refinement, not common with rebellious group

parts.note: rare is uncommon
a faction is a dissenting party

explanation.surface: Refinement is scarce among a mutinous clique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refinement' looks like elegance; here it is the physical sense of thinning out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarefaction is the making less dense of something, as of a gas, a purifying or thinning process.

clue.text: Source of river in Geneva?

parts.note: o' is a shortened form of of, as in o'clock
R is a standard abbreviation for river
i' is a dialect form of in
geneva is an old name for Dutch gin

explanation.surface: Asking where the river that runs through the Swiss city begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Geneva's capital hides the spirit: geneva, from the Dutch jenever, is gin. Both O and I come from apostrophised forms.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the starting point of something, the place it comes from.

clue.text: Stone Age tool I found in Scottish stream

indicators.note: what is found in something lies inside it

parts.note: a burn is a Scottish word for a brook
taken as written

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds a flint tool in a Highland stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A burin is a pointed flint chisel used for engraving in the Palaeolithic, a prehistoric implement.

clue.text: Larval excrement? With this it becomes pertness

indicators.note: becoming something else means one part is swapped for another

parts.note: sass is cheeky talk

explanation.surface: A grub's droppings, it seems, can turn into cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as FR AS S: the instruction says swap the FR for S, and the result is SASS. The wordplay depends on knowing the answer already.
explanation.definitionFit: Frass is the powdery waste left by insect larvae boring through wood or leaves.

clue.text: Female rarely round, once near

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
orby is a rare adjective for orbed or round

explanation.surface: A woman seldom visits, though once lived close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rarely' marks a rare word, not an infrequent act.
explanation.definitionFit: Forby is an archaic Scots word meaning beside or close at hand, so it once meant near.

clue.text: Gender, formerly, what may be hedged round say

indicators.note: going round something means enclosing it

parts.note: one hedges a bet to limit loss
e.g. means for example, like 'say'

explanation.surface: The old notion of gender is something you might hedge, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gender' is the old verb meaning to engender, not grammatical gender.
explanation.definitionFit: Gender was once a verb meaning to engender or procreate, the same as to beget offspring.

clue.text: Like dirty old jokes left aboard cruiser at sea?

indicators.note: something at sea is confused and tossed about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is short for left
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailors' smutty jokes left on board a cruiser out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The L is put aboard the ship's letters before they are all mixed. 'old' marks the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurrile is an archaic form of scurrilous, meaning grossly abusive or indecent, as coarse jokes are.

clue.text: So-called fern I omitted from headdress

indicators.note: a letter left out of a word is removed from it

parts.note: a tiara is a jewelled headband
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fern by that name is left off a bride's headdress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' means the fern is known by this name, not a separate wordplay element.
explanation.definitionFit: Tara is the New Zealand and Tasmanian name for the edible bracken fern, so a fern is called that.

clue.text: Wild horse dad found entering lake, small one

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
pa is a name for a father

explanation.surface: A wild horse finds a father figure wading into a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small one' qualifies the lake: a tarn is a small one.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarpan is an extinct wild horse of the Eurasian steppes.

clue.text: Love-drug provided by blade according to hearsay?

indicators.note: hearsay is what people hear spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a dagger is a short blade, said without the final R

explanation.surface: An aphrodisiac is said to come from a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: The match relies on a non-rhotic accent, which drops the final R. 'Love' hints at the hippie era of love and cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Dagga is the South African name for cannabis, a recreational drug.

clue.text: Shows disagreement casting initial V sign

indicators.note: casting off the opening letter, here specified, takes it away

parts.note: to vary is to differ

explanation.surface: Someone protests by flicking a rude V sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'V sign' looks like a rude gesture, but the V is the letter dropped and 'sign' is the definition. A V sign is a British insulting hand gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Increasingly plucky American, one in the groove

indicators.note: the single letter is put inside

parts.note: a gutter is a channel or groove
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An ever braver American is in the groove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the groove' reads as a happy idiom but places one inside a channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutty is American slang for courageous, and this is its comparative, meaning more spirited.

clue.text: Revelation from Calcutta narks may appear here

indicators.note: something revealed from within is exposed out of the words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A Calcutta informer exposes secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indian setting is apt: a tana, or thana, is an Indian police station, where police informers (narks) turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tana is a police station in India, the sort of place informers would visit.

clue.text: Strawberry runners? Means rat at work possibly

indicators.note: things at work are being processed, so the letters are worked into another order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sneaky rodent at work in the strawberry patch, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' suggests athletes; these are plant shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarmenta are slender runners sent out by plants such as strawberries, rooting at the nodes.
